clue.text: Son who behaved very deceitfully -— biblical book contains the account

indicators.note: contains says the book's name holds the abbreviation for account within it

parts.note: Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A scripture passage tells the story of a deceitful son.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis this son tricked his brother Esau out of his birthright and deceived his father Isaac.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genesis patriarch famously cheated his twin of his blessing by disguise.

clue.text: Control girl's credit

parts.note: Joy is a girl's name, here with its possessive S
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying 'on tick'

explanation.surface: A woman's borrowing gets checked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is everyday British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot's control lever in an aircraft, or a gaming controller, goes by this name.

clue.text: Returns chips

definitions.meaning: the tokens or chips used in board games and gambling

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means strikes back; as a plural noun it means gaming tokens.

clue.text: New York hobo and Cork boy connected somehow

indicators.note: New, read as an instruction, says the following letters are made into something new, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tramp from New York and an Irish lad from Cork are somehow linked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York' looks like one place, but 'New' is the anagram signal and only YORK is fodder; 'connected' is padding linking the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means by whatever method is needed, fair means or foul.

clue.text: Acceptable to snigger in the street? It's offensive!

parts.note: on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

indicators.note: in places the word for a snigger inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a snigger is a kind of laugh

explanation.surface: Someone sniggering in public is told it's offensive behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like an adjective about rudeness, but the definition is the noun: a military offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce, overwhelming attack is a military offensive.

clue.text: City appears extremely small through glasses

indicators.note: through says one piece runs inside the other, here within the pair of lenses

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of spectacles

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last, of the word small

explanation.surface: A city looks tiny when seen through binoculars or spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: OO is a crossword picture of a pair of glasses; inside it go S and L, the ends of 'small'.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Norway is a city.

clue.text: Denies cubs have been damaged by earth movement

indicators.note: have been damaged says the letters of the two words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone denies that young animals were hurt by a landslip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have been damaged' scrambles DENIES and CUBS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground sinking or settling is a movement of the earth that damages buildings.

clue.text: Almoner's oratory misrepresented honorary title

indicators.note: misrepresented says the letters are presented in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the S of the possessive counts as a letter here
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital social worker's speechmaking misstated someone's honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' rearranges ALMONERS and ORATORY; an almoner was a hospital social worker. The title is given to an eminent British astronomer.
explanation.definitionFit: The post is an honorary appointment held by a leading British astronomer.

clue.text: Sign, say, turned up on car

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
turned up in a down entry means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: EG (exempli gratia) means for example, i.e. say
the Mini is a classic small British car

explanation.surface: A signal, for instance, raised on top of a motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses EG to GE in this down entry; the Mini is a well-known small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins are one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Diatribe from bore, getting in paddy regularly

indicators.note: getting in says the picked letters go inside the word for bore

parts.note: to tire someone is to bore them

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of paddy, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A tedious person launches into a rant while in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like a temper tantrum (British slang), but only its alternate letters A and D are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech of denunciation is a diatribe.

clue.text: Place for kids to buy lunch is unusual, but not new

indicators.note: is unusual says the remaining letters come out in an unusual order
but not says a letter is removed from the phrase

explanation.surface: It's odd for a place for children to buy lunch, though not novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N from TO BUY LUNCH and rearrange the rest, as 'is unusual' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre offering leisure activities for teenagers is a place for children.

clue.text: Man attracting soldiers (the Isle, that is)

indicators.note: attracting means taking on a second piece next to the first

parts.note: Tim is a man's name
OR stands for other ranks, i.e. soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: The Isle of Man draws in troops, the parenthesis insists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' tempts one to think of the Isle of Man, but it is just a man's name; the ellipsis to the next clue is a distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Timor is an island in the Malay Archipelago shared by Indonesia and East Timor.

clue.text: … — volunteers — to races round circuit in military display

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
TT is the Tourist Trophy, the motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
O is round in shape
O is a circle, a circuit

explanation.surface: Volunteers go to motorcycle races around the track at an army show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tourist Trophy motorcycle races are held on the Isle of Man, tying this to the previous clue's 'Man'; 'to' just means next to, and the dashes are surface punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an evening military display of drill and music, like the Edinburgh one.

clue.text: Denied having popped off after receiving broadcast

indicators.note: after receiving says the word for popped off has taken in another word

parts.note: popped off is slang for died
broadcast seed has been sown, scattered widely

explanation.surface: Someone denied dying after a radio transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like radio, but means scattered, as seed is.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny a child or connection is to refuse to acknowledge it, to repudiate it.

clue.text: Treasury tags, for instance, are still spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of says the word for still is heard, and a same-sounding word is entered

parts.note: still means motionless, not moving

explanation.surface: Government finance labels are said to be unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: Treasury tags are the British office fasteners, cords with metal ends that hold punched papers together, not anything from the Treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasury tags are office supplies, examples of writing materials and desk sundries.

clue.text: Thickening of skin affecting horse, produced by maize

definitions.meaning: read literally: a corn (hardened skin) on the cob, a stocky horse
the ear of maize eaten as a vegetable

explanation.surface: A vet's note on a horse's callus somehow involves maize.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a joke: a corn is thickened skin, and a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear of sweetcorn, cooked and eaten whole, grows on the maize plant.

clue.text: He sends up gun, one put down in days of yore

indicators.note: put down in says the pieces are placed inside the word for former times

parts.note: days of yore are the past
rod is American slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Someone shoots a gun, and a person is killed in olden days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sends up' means mocks, not fires; rod is gangster slang for a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mocks by imitation, sending up others, writes or performs spoofs.

clue.text: Man and wife settled originally in the Isles

parts.note: he is a man, a male
a bride is a newly married wife

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of settled

explanation.surface: A married couple first set up home in some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes S from 'settled'. The Isles are the island groups off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The islands off western Scotland are often called simply the Western Isles.

clue.text: Ruined castle old couple circumnavigate in competition

parts.note: a brace is a pair, a couple

indicators.note: Ruined says the letters of castle are knocked about into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: A race over hurdles, nets and other barriers is a kind of competition.

clue.text: Beetle leaving mark on sailor

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A beetle leaves a mark on a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' is link padding: the beetle 'leaves' the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred dung beetle of ancient Egypt is a species of beetle.

clue.text: Somewhere to sleep with a girl

parts.note: a bunk on a ship or train is somewhere to sleep

explanation.surface: Somewhere to spend the night with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a female name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Force centres out of sort of apple and of lemon

clue.text: A serviceman assigned to the people's protection

clue.text: Flag is seen all round the state

indicators.note: seen all round says the word is goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A national flag can be seen all over the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner but is the plant: the yellow flag is a kind of wild iris.

clue.text: Reminiscent of the past, concierge retires after page leaves

clue.text: He won't be late, travelling by rail and road after the end of June

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled letters following the first letter picked
the end of picks the last letter of June
travelling says the letters move about into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges BY RAIL plus RD.

clue.text: Mice — billions are blind

parts.note: the blind lack eyes, read as a verb phrase

clue.text: Plant — something offered for sale to America
